name: 7 Easy Pieces wardrobe

card.summary: Donna Karan's 1985 concept of seven interchangeable basics built around a bodysuit that combine into a complete wardrobe, a model for capsule-style dressing.
card.note: A fashion concept from women's design; its use as a menswear template is informal.

quick.overview:
Seven Easy Pieces is the name given to Donna Karan's first collection concept in 1985: a small set of mix-and-match basics, centred on the bodysuit, designed to form a fully integrated wardrobe.

The appearance payoff is coherence. With fewer, compatible pieces, outfits are easier to put together and look consistent. The idea is a forerunner of capsule wardrobes that people use to simplify dressing.
quick.how: In practice people take the principle rather than the exact garments: choose a few versatile basics in a coordinated palette, make sure each works with the others, and rotate them. Karan has said she designed clothes she would wear herself, such as jersey dresses and opaque tights.
quick.risks: There are no health risks. The limits are practical: the original set was designed for women's wear in a particular era, and capsule approaches depend on fit and personal taste.

lead: Seven Easy Pieces was Donna Karan's debut women's collection concept in 1985, a set of interchangeable basics built around the bodysuit and designed to combine into a complete wardrobe [1]. She had launched her own label in 1984 after leaving Anne Klein [1].

The concept is cited as an early version of the capsule wardrobe: a small group of coordinated pieces that mix and match. People interested in dressing better with less use the principle to build looks that work together.
Published sources name the bodysuit as the centrepiece; this article does not list the remaining pieces because they are not given in the sources consulted.

chain: Mix and match them across outfits
A consistent, polished look with less effort
angle.text: A small set of compatible pieces makes outfits easier to coordinate, so the wearer looks put-together more consistently.

paras: Karan left Anne Klein in 1984 to found her own business with Stephan Weiss and Takihyo Corporation, aiming to design modern clothes for modern people [1]. Her 1985 First Collection included the Essentials line, which began as seven easy pieces built around the bodysuit [1].
She said she would design only clothes she would wear herself, such as jersey dresses and opaque Lycra tights [1].
The pieces were meant to be mixed and matched so that together they formed a fully integrated wardrobe [1].
